theorems.name: Annuity-Due Geometric Closed Form
theorems.description: Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} v^k = (1 - v^n)/(1 - v) for v ≠ 1. The annuity-due present value formula, mirror of the immediate-annuity case.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.Insurance

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

theorem annuityDue_closed_form_thm (v : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hv : v ≠ 1) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, v ^ k = (1 - v ^ n) / (1 - v) :=
  MathFin.annuityDue_closed_form v n hv

metadata.reference: Annuity-due formula (Bowers et al., Actuarial Mathematics)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export from MathFin. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Gompertz Cumulative Force of Mortality
theorems.description: ∫₀^t B·e^{c·u} du = (B/c)·(e^{c·t} - 1) for c ≠ 0. The closed-form cumulative force of mortality under the Gompertz law μ(t) = B·e^{c·t}.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.Mortality

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

theorem gompertz_cumulative_force_thm (B c t : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    ∫ u in (0:ℝ)..t, B * Real.exp (c * u) =
      (B / c) * (Real.exp (c * t) - 1) :=
  MathFin.gompertz_cumulative_force B c t hc

theorems.name: Compound-Poisson Aggregate-Loss MGF
theorems.description: For iid claim sizes Xᵢ, the MGF of the n-claim sum ∑_{i<n} Xᵢ, integrated against the Poisson(λ) law of n, equals exp(λ(M_X(t) − 1)). This is the compound-Poisson aggregate-loss MGF in mixture form: the claim count enters as the Poisson weights, not as a random variable N independent of the claims.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Probability.Jumps.CompoundPoissonMGF

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- **Compound-Poisson aggregate-loss MGF.** For a Poisson claim count `N ∼ Poisson(λ)` and
i.i.d. claim sizes `Xᵢ`, integrating the `n`-claim aggregate MGF against the Poisson law gives
`exp(λ·(M_X(t) − 1))` — the Poisson PGF evaluated at the common claim MGF. Re-exports
`MathFin.compoundPoisson_mgf`. -/
theorem compound_poisson_mgf
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    (lam : ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ) (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    ∫ n, mgf (fun ω => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) μ t ∂(poissonMeasure lam)
      = Real.exp ((lam : ℝ) * (mgf (X 0) μ t - 1)) :=
  MathFin.compoundPoisson_mgf lam t X hindep hident

metadata.reference: Compound Poisson MGF (Cramér-Lundberg actuarial theory)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof: n-claim iid-sum MGF (iIndepFun.mgf_sum) composed with the Poisson pgf (integral_pow_poissonMeasure). Re-export from MathFin. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Compound-Poisson Aggregate-Loss MGF with a Random Claim Count
theorems.description: For a claim count N ~ Poisson(λ) independent of i.i.d. claim sizes Xᵢ with E[exp(tX₀)] finite, the aggregate loss S = ∑_{i<N} Xᵢ has E[exp(tS)] = exp(λ(M_X(t) − 1)). The count is a random variable on the same probability space as the claims; the expectation over it is computed by freezing the count, which reduces it to the mixture form mf-compound-poisson-mgf.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Probability.Jumps.CompoundPoissonMGF

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **Compound-Poisson aggregate-loss MGF.** For `N ∼ Poisson(λ)` independent of i.i.d. claim
sizes `Xᵢ` whose MGF is finite at `t`, `𝔼[exp(t·∑_{i<N} Xᵢ)] = exp(λ·(M_X(t) − 1))`. -/
theorem compound_poisson_mgf_random_count_thm {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    (lam : ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ) {N : Ω → ℕ} (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hN : HasLaw N (poissonMeasure lam) μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hNX : IndepFun N (fun ω i ↦ X i ω) μ)
    (hint : Integrable (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (t * X 0 ω)) μ) :
    mgf (fun ω ↦ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N ω), X i ω) μ t
      = Real.exp ((lam : ℝ) * (mgf (X 0) μ t - 1)) :=
  MathFin.compoundPoisson_mgf_of_indepFun lam t X hN hindep hident hNX hint

metadata.reference: Compound Poisson MGF (Cramér-Lundberg actuarial theory); e.g. Klugman-Panjer-Willmot, Loss Models, Thm 9.3
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof: integrating out the independent Poisson count (integral_comp_of_hasLaw_of_countable, the freezing lemma for a countable variable), with E[exp(t·∑_{i<n} Xᵢ)] = M_X(t)ⁿ for each n (mgf_range_sum_of_iid, integrable by integrable_exp_mul_sum_range_of_iid) and n ↦ M_X(t)ⁿ integrable against Poisson(λ) (PoissonPgf.integrable_pow_poissonMeasure), then the mixture form compoundPoisson_mgf. The claim MGF must be finite at t (hint): otherwise E[exp(tS)] = +∞ when λ > 0, which the Bochner mgf records as 0, and the identity fails. Lives in MathFin/Probability/Jumps/CompoundPoissonMGF.lean, on MathFin/Probability/Analysis/IndepFreezing.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Survival Ratio tpₓ = S_X(x+t)/S_X(x)
theorems.description: Keystone of the survival model (Ito's ccdfTx_ccdfX): the conditional survival probability tpₓ = P(X>x+t | X>x) equals the ratio S_X(x+t)/S_X(x) of unconditional survival probabilities, for t ≥ 0.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.SurvivalModel

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin.SurvivalModel

/-- **Survival ratio** `tpₓ = S_X(x+t) / S_X(x)` for `t ≥ 0` — the keystone of the
survival model (Ito's `ccdfTx_ccdfX`): conditioning on survival to age `x`, a further
`t` years of survival has probability the ratio of the two unconditional survival
probabilities. Re-exports `MathFin.SurvivalModel.survive_eq_survivalFunction_div`. -/
theorem survival_ratio
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ}
    (hX : Measurable X) (x : ℝ) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    survive P X t x = survivalFunction P X (x + t) / survivalFunction P X x :=
  MathFin.SurvivalModel.survive_eq_survivalFunction_div hX x ht

metadata.reference: Yosuke Ito, AFP Actuarial Mathematics, Survival_Model (ccdfTx_ccdfX)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, our own design: the conditional survival probability, defined via Mathlib's conditional measure cond, collapses to the survival-function ratio through cond_apply and the sub-event alive(x+t) ⊆ alive(x). The AFP entry (Ito, Actuarial Mathematics, Survival_Model) was consulted as a source and is cited. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Survival Function at Age Zero S_X(0)=1
theorems.description: Ito's ccdfX_0_1: the survival function of the age at death is 1 at age 0, since X > 0 almost surely.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.SurvivalModel

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin.SurvivalModel

/-- **`S_X(0) = 1`**: everyone is alive at age `0`, since the age at death `X > 0`
almost surely — Ito's `ccdfX_0_1`. Re-exports `MathFin.SurvivalModel.survivalFunction_zero`. -/
theorem survival_at_zero
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ}
    (hpos : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, 0 < X ω) :
    survivalFunction P X 0 = 1 :=
  MathFin.SurvivalModel.survivalFunction_zero hpos

theorems.name: Formalize the classical loaded premium principles (expected-value, variance, standard-deviation) and their nonnegative-loading bounds
theorems.description: Classical loaded premium principles and their nonnegative-loading bounds: each prices at or above the pure premium.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.ActuarialInsurance

open MathFin

/-- The three classical loaded premium principles with nonnegative loadings price at or above the pure premium (the mean loss). -/
theorem mf_insurance_premium_principles (μ σ2 σ θ α β : ℝ) (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hσ2 : 0 ≤ σ2)
    (hσ : 0 ≤ σ) (hθ : 0 ≤ θ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) :
    expectedValuePremium θ μ ≥ μ ∧ variancePremium α μ σ2 ≥ μ ∧ stdDevPremium β μ σ ≥ μ :=
  MathFin.premium_ge_mean μ σ2 σ θ α β hμ hσ2 hσ hθ hα hβ

theorems.name: Life Annuity-Due Under a Constant Force of Mortality
theorems.description: With flat-rate discount factors B(0, k) = e^{−rk} (zero-coupon bond prices) and survival probabilities S(k) = exp(−∫₀ᵏ μ) for a constant force of mortality μ ≡ m, the n-payment life annuity-due Σ_{k<n} B(0, k)·S(k) equals (1 − vⁿ)/(1 − v) with v = e^{−(r+m)}, provided v ≠ 1: a constant force of mortality acts as an addition to the interest rate. The life annuity-due is defined as this sum; its identification with the value of the payments made while a random lifetime has not ended is the entry mf-life-annuity-due-is-contract-value.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.Insurance

open MathFin

/-- Under a constant force of mortality `m`, the life annuity-due is the annuity-certain at the
discount factor `e^{−(r + m)}`. -/
theorem life_annuity_due_constant_force_thm {r m : ℝ} (n : ℕ)
    (hv : Real.exp (-(r + m)) ≠ 1) :
    lifeAnnuityDue r (fun _ ↦ m) n =
      (1 - Real.exp (-(r + m)) ^ n) / (1 - Real.exp (-(r + m))) :=
  lifeAnnuityDue_const n hv

metadata.reference: D. C. M. Dickson, M. R. Hardy and H. R. Waters, Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent Risks, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Chapter 5 (annuities)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.lifeAnnuityDue_const (MathFin/Insurance/Insurance.lean). lifeAnnuityDue r μ n := Σ_{k<n} zcb r 0 k · survivalFromForce μ k, with zcb from MathFin/Models/Rates/ZCB.lean and survivalFromForce from MathFin/Insurance/Mortality.lean; the closed form is the annuity-due geometric sum annuityDue_closed_form at v = e^{−(r+m)}. SCOPE: constant force of mortality and flat rate; the probabilistic reading of the sum as the value of payments to a random lifetime is lifeAnnuityDue_eq_value (MathFin/Insurance/AnnuityValue.lean), a separate entry.

theorems.name: The Life Annuity-Due Is the Value of Payments Made While the Default Indicator of the Lifetime Is Zero
theorems.description: Let tau be a measurable lifetime under a probability measure Q whose survival probabilities S_tau(k) = Q(tau > k) at the dates k < n are those of a force of mortality mu, survivalFromForce mu k. Then the life annuity-due of n payments, the sum over k < n of the flat-rate zero-coupon bond price zcb r 0 k times survivalFromForce mu k (lifeAnnuityDue), is the value (Contract.value) under Q, on the deterministic flat-rate discount t -> zcb r 0 t, of the contract that pays one at each date k < n while the default indicator 1{tau <= k} of the lifetime is still zero (the schedule of payments payFlows of 1 - 1{tau <= k}). The value is under the law of the lifetime: no market is involved, and the survival probabilities at the other dates are not used.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.AnnuityValue

open MeasureTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts
open scoped NNReal

/-- The life annuity-due is the value, on the flat-rate discount, of the payments of one made
while the default indicator of the lifetime is zero. -/
theorem life_annuity_due_is_contract_value {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {τ : Ω → ℝ} (hτ : Measurable τ) (r : ℝ) (μ : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hS : ∀ k < n, SurvivalModel.survivalFunction Q τ k = survivalFromForce μ k) :
    lifeAnnuityDue r μ n =
      (payFlows (fun k ↦ (k : ℝ≥0)) (fun k ↦ (.sub (.const 1) (.obs () k) : Payoff Unit)) n).value
        Q (fun t _ ↦ zcb r 0 t) (defaultIndicator τ) :=
  lifeAnnuityDue_eq_value Q hτ r μ n hS

metadata.reference: D. C. M. Dickson, M. R. Hardy and H. R. Waters, Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent Risks, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Chapter 5 (annuities)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the statement as written. lifeAnnuityDue_eq_value in MathFin/Insurance/AnnuityValue.lean: along every scenario the schedule is worth the sum of the discounted payoffs (pathPV_payFlows), the integral of the sum is the sum of the integrals, and the integral of 1 - 1{tau <= k} is 1 - Q(tau <= k), which is the survival function at k (probReal_compl_eq_one_sub); the contract is the one of the credit module (defaultIndicator, Models/Credit/DefaultTime.lean). SCOPE: a deterministic discount and a lifetime under Q; the identification is for the dates k < n at which the survival function is that of the force of mortality. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: The Esscher Premium Is the Price of the Loss Under the Esscher Pricing Measure of the Insured Market
theorems.description: Let X be a measurable loss under a probability measure P with e^(hX) and X e^(hX) integrable. In the insured market (insuredMarket: the one-date market with the unit numeraire in which the loss is quoted at its Esscher premium E[X e^(hX)] / E[e^(hX)] until the date T and equals X at T), the Esscher tilt of P with density e^(hX)/E[e^(hX)] is a pricing measure (Market.IsPricingMeasure at T), and under it the market's price (Market.price) of the claim paying the loss at T is the Esscher premium E[X e^(hX)] / E[e^(hX)]. The market is built to quote the loss at that premium and has no dynamics before T. For an arbitrary market with the unit numeraire the same price identity holds for the claim paying the asset at T under the Esscher tilt of its reference measure (esscherPremium_eq_price, a library lemma not restated in this entry).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.EsscherPremium

open MeasureTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts
open scoped NNReal

/-- The Esscher tilt is a pricing measure of the insured market, and under it the loss is worth
the Esscher premium. -/
theorem esscher_premium_is_price {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ}
    (hX : Measurable X) {h : ℝ} (hexp : Integrable (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (h * X ω)) P)
    (hXexp : Integrable (fun ω ↦ X ω * Real.exp (h * X ω)) P) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    (insuredMarket P hX h T).IsPricingMeasure T (P.tilted fun ω ↦ h * X ω) ∧
      (insuredMarket P hX h T).price (P.tilted fun ω ↦ h * X ω) (.pay T (.obs () T))
        = (∫ ω, X ω * Real.exp (h * X ω) ∂P) / ∫ ω, Real.exp (h * X ω) ∂P :=
  ⟨isPricingMeasure_insuredMarket_tilted hX hexp hXexp T, price_insuredMarket_tilted hX T⟩

metadata.reference: Gerber and Shiu, Option pricing by Esscher transforms (1994); Esscher, On the probability function in the collective theory of risk (1932)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the statement as written. isPricingMeasure_insuredMarket_tilted and price_insuredMarket_tilted in MathFin/Insurance/EsscherPremium.lean, on the one-date market Market.oneDate (MathFin/Pricing/OneDateMarket.lean) with its initial price the Esscher premium: the tilt is a probability measure equivalent to P (isProbabilityMeasure_tilted, tilted_absolutelyContinuous, absolutelyContinuous_tilted), X is integrable under it (integrable_tilted_iff) with mean the premium (integral_tilted_eq_esscherPremium), and a measure with those properties prices the one-date market (Market.isPricingMeasure_oneDate). The general price identity for an arbitrary market with unit numeraire is esscherPremium_eq_price in the same module. SCOPE: the insured market quotes the loss at the Esscher premium by construction, and there is no dynamics before T; the statement does not derive the premium from a hedging or equilibrium argument. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: An Esscher Tilt Prices the Insured Market Exactly When Its Premium Is the Market Quote
theorems.description: Let X be a measurable loss under a probability measure P, T > 0 a date, and h, h' two Esscher parameters with e^(h'X) and X e^(h'X) integrable. In the insured market of parameter h (insuredMarket: the one-date market with the unit numeraire in which the loss is quoted at its Esscher premium for h until T and equals X at T), the Esscher tilt of P with parameter h' is a pricing measure (Market.IsPricingMeasure at T) if and only if the Esscher premium for h' equals the Esscher premium for h. So the pricing measure fixes the premium, not the parameter. No integrability is assumed for h: when E[e^(hX)] or E[X e^(hX)] is not finite, the quote is the Bochner integral's junk value, and the statement is about that number. Strict monotonicity of the premium in the parameter, which would give h' = h for a non-degenerate loss, is not proved.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.EsscherPremium

open MeasureTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts
open scoped NNReal

/-- The `h'`-Esscher tilt prices the insured market of parameter `h` exactly when the premiums
agree. -/
theorem esscher_tilt_prices_insured_market_iff {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ} (hX : Measurable X) {h h' : ℝ} {T : ℝ≥0} (hT : 0 < T)
    (hexp : Integrable (fun ω ↦ Real.exp (h' * X ω)) P)
    (hXexp : Integrable (fun ω ↦ X ω * Real.exp (h' * X ω)) P) :
    (insuredMarket P hX h T).IsPricingMeasure T (P.tilted fun ω ↦ h' * X ω)
      ↔ esscherPremium P X h' = esscherPremium P X h :=
  isPricingMeasure_insuredMarket_tilted_iff hX hT hexp hXexp

metadata.reference: Gerber and Shiu, Option pricing by Esscher transforms (1994); Esscher, On the probability function in the collective theory of risk (1932)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the statement as written. isPricingMeasure_insuredMarket_tilted_iff in MathFin/Insurance/EsscherPremium.lean: the forward direction is Market.integral_eq_of_isPricingMeasure_oneDate (MathFin/Pricing/OneDateMarket.lean), where the martingale property of the deflated asset between 0 and T keeps its mean (Martingale.setIntegral_eq), combined with the mean of X under the tilt being the premium (integral_tilted_eq_esscherPremium); the converse is Market.isPricingMeasure_oneDate. SCOPE: the hypothesis T > 0 is needed (at T = 0 the quote is never read); uniqueness of the parameter (strict monotonicity of the premium in h) is not proved; the insured market quotes the loss at the Esscher premium by construction and has no dynamics before T. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Conditional Survival in a Finite Life Table Is the Table Ratio
theorems.description: Let l be a finite life table on ages 0..n with l_0 > 0, nonincreasing (l_{k+1} <= l_k for k < n) and nonnegative. Its probability law lifeTableMeasure n l on Fin (n+1) puts mass (l_i - l_{i+1})/l_0 on the death cell i < n and l_n/l_0 on the residual outcome n, and lifeTableLifetime n reads the lifetime i+1 off the outcome i (the residual survivor at n+1). Then for ages x and k with x + k <= n, the probability that a life aged x survives k further years (survive, the conditional probability P(T > x + k | T > x)) is l_{x+k}/l_x. No positivity of l_x is assumed: when l_x = 0 both sides are 0 (division by zero), the conditional probability being that of a null event.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.SurvivalModel

open MathFin.SurvivalModel

/-- The conditional survival probability of the life-table law is the table ratio. -/
theorem life_table_survival_ratio (n : ℕ) (l : ℕ → ℝ) (hl0 : 0 < l 0)
    (hmono : ∀ k < n, l (k + 1) ≤ l k) (hnonneg : ∀ k ≤ n, 0 ≤ l k) (x k : ℕ)
    (hxk : x + k ≤ n) :
    survive (lifeTableMeasure n l) (lifeTableLifetime n) k x = l (x + k) / l x :=
  survive_lifeTable n l hl0 hmono hnonneg x k hxk

metadata.reference: D. C. M. Dickson, M. R. Hardy and H. R. Waters, Actuarial Mathematics for Life Contingent Risks, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2013), Chapter 3 (life tables)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the statement as written. survive_lifeTable in MathFin/Insurance/SurvivalModel.lean: the survival function of the life-table law at an integer date m <= n is l_m/l_0 (survivalFunction_lifeTable: the integral of the indicator against the finite weights Measure.ofWeights of MathFin/Probability/Laws/FiniteWeights.lean, the weights telescoping over the cells m..n-1 plus the residual), and the conditional survival is the ratio of survival functions (survive_eq_survivalFunction_div). SCOPE: a finite table with the survivors of the last age kept as one residual outcome at n + 1; integer ages and durations; the table is an input, there is no mortality law behind it. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Term Insurance Plus Pure Endowment Is One Minus d Times the Life Annuity-Due
theorems.description: Let tau be a measurable lifetime, positive almost surely, under a probability measure Q, and r a flat rate. On the deterministic discount t -> zcb r 0 t, with the default indicator 1{tau <= u} as the observed process, the value (Contract.value) of the n-year term insurance, the protection leg cdsProtectionLeg of the unit grid at recovery 0 (one paid at the end of the year of death if death occurs within n years), plus the value of the n-year pure endowment (one paid at time n if tau > n), equals 1 - (1 - e^{-r}) times the value of the n-year life annuity-due (payFlows of one at each date k < n while 1{tau <= k} is zero): A^1_{x:n} + nEx = 1 - d a_{x:n}, with d = 1 - e^{-r}. No condition on r.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.AnnuityValue

open MeasureTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts
open scoped NNReal

/-- Term insurance plus pure endowment is `1 − d` times the life annuity-due, in the values of the
contracts. -/
theorem term_insurance_plus_pure_endowment {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {τ : Ω → ℝ} (hτ : Measurable τ)
    (hpos : ∀ᵐ ω ∂Q, 0 < τ ω) (r : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    (cdsProtectionLeg (fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ≥0)) 0 n).value Q (fun t _ ↦ zcb r 0 t)
        (defaultIndicator τ)
      + (Contract.pay (n : ℝ≥0) (.sub (.const 1) (.obs () (n : ℝ≥0)) : Payoff Unit)).value Q
          (fun t _ ↦ zcb r 0 t) (defaultIndicator τ)
      = 1 - (1 - Real.exp (-r)) *
          (payFlows (fun k ↦ (k : ℝ≥0)) (fun k ↦ (.sub (.const 1) (.obs () k) : Payoff Unit)) n).value
            Q (fun t _ ↦ zcb r 0 t) (defaultIndicator τ) :=
  termInsurance_add_pureEndowment_eq Q hτ hpos r n

theorems.name: Whole-Life Insurance Is One Minus d Times the Life Annuity-Due
theorems.description: Let tau be a measurable lifetime, positive almost surely, under a probability measure Q, with survival function S(k) = Q(tau > k), and r > 0 a flat rate (bond price zcb r 0 k = e^{-rk} at integer dates). As n → ∞ the value of the n-year life annuity-due contract tends to ä = Σ_{k ≥ 0} e^{-rk} S(k), and the value of the n-year term insurance contract (one paid at the end of the year of death) tends to 1 − (1 − e^{-r}) ä: whole-life insurance is A = 1 − d ä with d = 1 − e^{-r}. No summability is assumed; both series converge by comparison with the geometric series of e^{-r} < 1.

/-- Whole-life insurance and the whole-life annuity-due as limits of term contract values, with

theorem whole_life_insurance_annuity_due {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {τ : Ω → ℝ} (hτ : Measurable τ)
    (hpos : ∀ᵐ ω ∂Q, 0 < τ ω) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ (lifeAnnuityFlows n).value Q (fun s _ ↦ zcb r 0 s) (defaultIndicator τ))
        atTop (𝓝 (∑' k : ℕ, zcb r 0 k * SurvivalModel.survivalFunction Q τ k)) ∧

  ⟨tendsto_value_lifeAnnuityFlows Q hτ hr, tendsto_value_termInsurance Q hτ hpos hr⟩

theorems.name: Last-Survivor Annuity Is the Sum of the Single-Life Values Minus the Joint-Life Value
theorems.description: Let T1 and T2 be two measurable lifetimes under a probability measure Q, D a deterministic discount, t_k payment dates and b_k payment amounts for k < n. The model observes the default indicator 1{T_i <= u} of each life (index true for T1, false for T2). The schedule payFlows paying b_k at t_k while either life survives, the payoff b_k * max(1 - 1{T1 <= t_k}, 1 - 1{T2 <= t_k}), is worth, as a Contract.value under Q on the discount D, the value of the schedule paying b_k while life 1 survives plus the value of the schedule paying b_k while life 2 survives minus the value of the schedule paying b_k while both survive (the min of the two survival payoffs). No independence between the lives is assumed.

import MathFin.Insurance.AnnuityValue

open MeasureTheory MathFin MathFin.Contracts
open scoped NNReal

/-- The last-survivor annuity is the sum of the single-life annuities minus the joint-life annuity. -/
theorem last_survivor_annuity_value {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] (T1 T2 : Ω → ℝ)
    (hT1 : Measurable T1) (hT2 : Measurable T2) (D : ℝ≥0 → ℝ) (t : ℕ → ℝ≥0)
    (b : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    (payFlows t (fun k ↦ .mul (.const (b k))
      (.max (.sub (.const 1) (.obs true (t k))) (.sub (.const 1) (.obs false (t k))))) n).value
        Q (fun s _ ↦ D s) (fun i ↦ defaultIndicator (bif i then T1 else T2) ())
      = (payFlows t (fun k ↦ .mul (.const (b k))
          (.sub (.const 1) (.obs true (t k)))) n).value
          Q (fun s _ ↦ D s) (fun i ↦ defaultIndicator (bif i then T1 else T2) ())
        + (payFlows t (fun k ↦ .mul (.const (b k))
            (.sub (.const 1) (.obs false (t k)))) n).value
            Q (fun s _ ↦ D s) (fun i ↦ defaultIndicator (bif i then T1 else T2) ())
        - (payFlows t (fun k ↦ .mul (.const (b k))
            (.min (.sub (.const 1) (.obs true (t k)))
              (.sub (.const 1) (.obs false (t k))))) n).value
            Q (fun s _ ↦ D s) (fun i ↦ defaultIndicator (bif i then T1 else T2) ()) := lastSurvivor_annuity_eq_value Q T1 T2 hT1 hT2 D t b n

theorems.name: Thiele's Differential Equation for the Prospective Reserve
theorems.description: Let delta (force of interest), mu (force of mortality), prem (premium rate) and b (death benefit) be continuous on [0, T] with T > 0, and g a terminal payment. The prospective reserve V(t) = integral_t^T F(t, s) (mu(s) b(s) - prem(s)) ds + F(t, T) g, with F(t, s) = exp(-integral_t^s delta) * hazardSurvival mu s / hazardSurvival mu t the discount at delta times the survival factor from t to s under the force mu (a probability when mu ≥ 0) (thieleReserve, thieleFactor), is differentiable at every t in (0, T) with V'(t) = (delta(t) + mu(t)) V(t) + prem(t) - mu(t) b(t). Only the differential equation is proved; the discrete one-step recursion for the reserve is not.

import MathFin.Insurance.Mortality

open MathFin

/-- Thiele's differential equation for the prospective reserve. -/
theorem thiele_reserve_ode (δ μ prem b : ℝ → ℝ) (g T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hδ : ContinuousOn δ (Set.Icc 0 T)) (hμ : ContinuousOn μ (Set.Icc 0 T))
    (hprem : ContinuousOn prem (Set.Icc 0 T)) (hb : ContinuousOn b (Set.Icc 0 T))
    (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 < t) (htT : t < T) :
    HasDerivAt (thieleReserve δ μ prem b g T)
      ((δ t + μ t) * thieleReserve δ μ prem b g T t + prem t - μ t * b t) t :=
  hasDerivAt_thieleReserve δ μ prem b g T hT hδ hμ hprem hb t ht0 htT

theorems.name: Bühlmann Observations Are a Single-Index Model: Shocks Uncorrelated with the Hypothetical Mean and with Each Other
theorems.description: In the finite latent mixture (prior weights p on a finite parameter set, n observations iid given the parameter with weights w, observation function v), write each observation as X_i = m(Θ) + ε_i with m(Θ) the hypothetical mean and ε_i = X_i - m(Θ). For every i, cov(m(Θ), ε_i) = 0, for i ≠ j, cov(ε_i, ε_j) = 0, and Var ε_i = E[σ²(Θ)], the expected process variance: the single-index structure of Sharpe's model with the hypothetical mean as the factor with loading 1.

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory MathFin

theorem buhlmann_shocks {Θ Ξ : Type*} [Fintype Θ] [Fintype Ξ] [MeasurableSpace Θ] [MeasurableSpace Ξ]

      ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → cov[shock n w v i, shock n w v j; mixtureLaw n p w] = 0)
      ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, Var[shock n w v i; mixtureLaw n p w] = expectedProcessVariance p w v :=
  ⟨covariance_latentMean_shock hm, fun _ _ hij ↦ covariance_shock_shock hm hij,
    variance_shock hm⟩

theorems.name: Chain-Ladder Completion by the Selected Factors
theorems.description: For a cumulative run-off triangle C with n development periods, let f̂_j be the chain-ladder factor (the ratio of the column-(j+1) sum to the column-j sum over the rows observed in both) and let the completion keep observed cells (i + j ≤ n) and multiply forward by f̂ on the others. On every unobserved cell the completion equals C(i, n − i) · ∏_{n−i ≤ k < j} f̂_k, the prediction of the row's value at j from its last observed value. If the triangle is nonnegative, its rows are nondecreasing on observed cells and every factor denominator is positive, the completed ultimate is at least the last observed value, so the predicted outstanding claims are nonnegative.

open MathFin

/-- The chain-ladder completion of a triangle is the prediction by the selected factors on every
unobserved cell, and with monotone nonnegative rows and positive denominators the completed
ultimate is at least the last observed value. -/
theorem chain_ladder_completion (n : ℕ) (C : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) :
    (∀ i j, n < i + j →
      chainComplete n C i j = chainPrediction (chainFactor n C) (C i) j (n - i)) ∧
    ((∀ i j, 0 ≤ C i j) → (∀ i j, i + (j + 1) ≤ n → C i j ≤ C i (j + 1)) →
      (∀ j < n, 0 < ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n - j), C i j) →
      ∀ i, C i (n - i) ≤ chainComplete n C i n) :=
  ⟨chainComplete_eq_chainPrediction n C, fun hC hmono hdenom ↦ le_chainComplete n C hC hmono hdenom⟩

theorems.name: Mack's Model: the Chain-Ladder Predictions Are a Martingale

theorems.name: Exact Rational Chain Ladder Certifies the Real Completion

When every factor denominator within the horizon is nonzero, the evaluator returns a value at every cell with j ≤ n.

theorems.name: Lundberg's Inequality for a Random-Walk Surplus
theorems.description: For a surplus U_n = u + Σ_{k<n} Y_k with i.i.d. measurable increments Y_k and a real R > 0 with E[exp(−R·Y_0)] = 1, the probability that U_n < 0 for some n is at most exp(−R·u). It holds for every real u and uses no assumption on E[Y_0]; the adjustment coefficient R is a hypothesis, not constructed. This is the discrete-time (random-walk) statement, not the continuous-time Cramér–Lundberg ruin probability.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Insurance.Lundberg

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory MathFin

theorem lundberg_inequality_random_walk {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {R : ℝ} (u : ℝ) (hY : ∀ k, Measurable (Y k))
    (hindep : iIndepFun Y P) (hident : ∀ k, IdentDistrib (Y k) (Y 0) P P) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hadj : mgf (Y 0) P (-R) = 1) :
    P {ω | ∃ n, u + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, Y k ω < 0} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-R * u)) :=
  lundberg_inequality u hY hindep hident hR hadj

metadata.reference: Lundberg's inequality (Asmussen and Albrecher, Ruin Probabilities)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the statement as written, in MathFin/Insurance/Lundberg.lean: the exponential e^{−R U_n} is a martingale for the increment filtration (martingale_exp_sub_of_indep_increments), Doob's maximal inequality bounds the probability of reaching 1, and ruin is the increasing union of the bounded events. Discrete time only; the adjustment coefficient is assumed, not constructed, and E[Y_0] > 0 is not used.

theorems.name: Lundberg Bound for the Cramér–Lundberg Embedded Walk
theorems.description: For a positive premium rate c, a positive arrival rate λ, and measurable waiting times T_k and claims X_k whose gaps c·T_k − X_k are i.i.d., with T_0 independent of X_0, T_0 having the law Exp(λ) and R > 0 solving λ(E[exp(R·X_0)] − 1) − c·R = 0, the probability that the surplus u + Σ_{k<n}(c·T_k − X_k) after some claim is negative is at most exp(−R·u). It concerns the embedded random walk at claim instants; no Poisson process is constructed and the link to continuous-time ruin is not formalised.

import MathFin.Insurance.CramerLundberg

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory MathFin

theorem cramer_lundberg_embedded_ruin {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {T X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {lam c R : ℝ} (u : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam)
    (hc : 0 < c) (hR : 0 < R) (hTm : ∀ k, Measurable (T k)) (hXm : ∀ k, Measurable (X k))
    (hindep : iIndepFun (fun k ω ↦ c * T k ω - X k ω) P)
    (hident : ∀ k, IdentDistrib (fun ω ↦ c * T k ω - X k ω) (fun ω ↦ c * T 0 ω - X 0 ω) P P)
    (hpair : IndepFun (T 0) (X 0) P) (hT : HasLaw (T 0) (expMeasure lam) P)
    (hadj : IsLundbergAdjustmentCoefficient lam c R fun r ↦ mgf (X 0) P r) :
    P {ω | ∃ n, u + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (c * T k ω - X k ω) < 0}
      ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-R * u)) :=
  cramerLundberg_embedded_ruin_le u hlam hc hR hTm hXm hindep hident hpair hT hadj

metadata.reference: Cramér–Lundberg model (Asmussen and Albrecher, Ruin Probabilities)
metadata.formalization_scope: Reduced core: the embedded-walk bound in MathFin/Insurance/CramerLundberg.lean, composed from lundberg_inequality and the equivalence of the walk's adjustment equation with the Cramér–Lundberg equation. The Exp(λ) Laplace transform E[exp(−a·T_0)] = λ/(λ + a) is proved (MathFin/Probability/Laws/ExponentialMGF.lean) from the law of T_0, which is assumed only for the first waiting time. Not proved: the Poisson process producing the i.i.d. waiting times, and the equality of the embedded walk's ruin probability with that of the continuous-time surplus process.
